page: Microsoft Azure D4lds_v6 is a low-memory, local-disk-enabled virtual machine instance belonging to the Dldsv6 server family. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, this instance features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance includes a 236 GB local disk and supports Premium Storage, while running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong single-core profile, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2141.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.32 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show clear performance tradeoffs. The instance registers a weak multi-core stress-ng score of 3990.56 and a weak Passmark memory score of 1693.71, alongside lower read-only memory bandwidth. Despite these memory constraints, the processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), enable average performance in LLM prompt processing and text generation for small models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D4lds_v6 offers a budget-friendly entry point for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints. The low memory-to-vCPU ratio reduces overhead costs compared to standard general-purpose instances. This hardware profile is best suited for single-threaded applications, lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and entry-level utility services. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, large-scale software compilation, or heavy multi-threaded parallel processing.
